description: Sourcing verdicts for third-party sources. A rule here is a decision that has already been made and argued in a docs/SOURCING-REPORT*.md: it blocks a host (or a repository, or a feed name) from becoming an OmniSource source, from being promoted out of the discovery store, and from being referenced by catalog.json. It does not mark anything as safe: a source with no rule is still reviewed by a human, exactly as before.

rules.description: Account-gated 'decrypted app store' frontpages that redistribute FairPlay-stripped copies of App Store apps (ARM Store and the other FMHY 'Decrypted App Store' links).
rules.reason: no machine-readable AltStore/Feather feed, no developer-published download link or digest, sign-in required to reach any catalogue, and the binaries are re-released copies of other people's apps rather than the publisher's own build - so nothing about them can be attributed, verified or re-verified.

rules.description: Aggregator feeds and IPA libraries that re-host tweaked or decrypted builds collected from elsewhere, including GitHub repositories whose only content is other people's .ipa files.
rules.reason: an aggregator is not the developer's release channel: the build, its version and its signature are chosen by whoever re-uploaded it, so provenance cannot be established or maintained from here. Where the same app has a real upstream, catalog that upstream instead.

rules.description: Repositories and archives whose purpose is distributing cracked, paid-for-free or abandoned commercial software rather than their own builds.
rules.reason: distributing paid software without the developer's consent is out of scope for this project, and a catalogue built on it could not survive the first takedown; these feeds are also where injected adware historically shows up.
